h1: Rigid-Flex PCB Layout Design Guidelines: Best Practices for Reliable PCB Layout

headings.text: Rigid-Flex PCB Layout Design Guidelines: Best Practices for Reliable PCB Layout
Substrate Selection and PCB Stackup Design
1. Choose the Right Flexible Substrate
2. Design the PCB Stackup Separately for Rigid and Flexible Areas
3. Use Rolled Annealed Copper for Dynamic Flex Areas
4. Create Smooth Layer Transitions
PCB Layout Rules for Rigid and Flexible Areas
1. Place Components Only in Rigid Sections
2. Keep Routing Away from the Neutral Bend Axis
3. Avoid Vias and Large Copper Features in Bend Areas
4. Route Traces Perpendicular to the Bend Direction
5. Maintain Uniform Trace Width and Spacing
PCB Routing Guidelines for Flex Regions
1. Use Rounded Trace Corners
2. Increase Trace Width in Dynamic Bend Areas
3. Preserve Differential Pair Integrity
4. Eliminate Branch Routing
5. Keep Flex Routing as Short as Possible
Via and Pad Design Guidelines
1. Minimize Vias in Flexible Areas
2. Keep Transition Vias Away from the Rigid-Flex Boundary
3. Use Oval Pads for Flexible Circuits
4. Taper Traces Across the Rigid-Flex Transition
5. Place COB Pads and Gold Fingers Only in Rigid Areas
Grounding, Copper Pour, and EMI Shielding
1. Avoid Solid Copper Pours in Dynamic Bend Areas
2. Keep Full Ground Planes in Rigid Sections
3. Place Ground Vias in Rigid Areas
4. Keep Ground Splits Away from the Transition Zone
Impedance Control and High-Speed PCB Layout
1. Calculate Impedance Separately for Rigid and Flexible Sections
2. Simulate Signal Transitions Across the Rigid-Flex Interface
3. Keep High-Speed Flex Routing Short
4. Account for Impedance Changes After Assembly
Mechanical Design and Assembly Considerations
1. Use Rounded Board Outlines
2. Add Stiffeners Under Components and Connectors
3. Allow Appropriate Dimensional Tolerance
4. Follow Minimum Bend Radius Requirements
5. Reinforce Gold Finger Areas
Surface Finish and Solder Mask Guidelines
1. Use Flexible Solder Mask in Bend Areas
2. Minimize Solder Mask Openings
3. ENIG Is the Preferred Surface Finish
4. Keep Silkscreen Away from Bend Areas
Thermal Design Considerations
1. Place Heat-Generating Components in Rigid Areas
2. Do Not Extend Thermal Structures into Flex Sections
3. Keep Flexible Areas Away from Heat Sources
DFM Guidelines for Rigid-Flex PCB Manufacturing
1. Follow Appropriate Design Rules
2. Include Process Rails and Support Tabs
3. Optimize Lamination Parameters
4. Use Laser Routing for Depanelization
5. Provide Clearance Beneath Flexible Sections
Reliability and Environmental Design
1. Design for Vibration Resistance
2. Allow Stress Relief for Thermal Expansion
3. Improve Moisture Protection
4. Verify Bend Life Early in the Design Stage
Common Rigid-Flex PCB Layout Mistakes to Avoid
Conclusion
